negative_findings.description: No vendor case study explicitly scoped to a Slovak bank ATM deployment was found on Diebold Nixdorf's or NCR Atleos's public case-study libraries. The closest CEE evidence is the Diebold Nixdorf CSOB case study (end-to-end ATM outsourcing, 99.8% uptime, ~20-year relationship) which does not state whether the Slovak arm is in scope, and the bank99 (Austria) ATM-as-a-Service case.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: The core hypothesis of this cell - that OEMs quantify Slovak deployments - is only weakly supported for the two largest ATM OEMs; SK evidence has to come via the channel partner (Printec) and via competition filings instead.

negative_findings.description: No public Printec Slovakia customer/reference page naming individual Slovak banks was located. negative_findings.description: SK business press (Forbes.sk, reprinted by Asseco) reports that Slovak banks deliberately present vendor-built digital innovations as their own and in some cases contractually require suppliers NOT to list them as references.
negative_findings.result_summary: Confirmed as an explicitly reported market norm, not merely an observation of missing data.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This caps the achievable yield of the vendor-reference route and argues for weighting registers, competition filings, tenders and financial statements more heavily than vendor marketing pages.

negative_findings.description: No SK-named customer was found for card-management/switching platform vendors (OpenWay Way4, Tietoevry, Monet+, SIA/Nexi processing). Searches returned only BG/other-CEE references.

negative_findings.description: No formal SK vendor/partner directory for banking technology (e.g. a Slovak Banking Association supplier register or an ITAS-style banking-tech member list) was identified in this pass; the closest functional equivalents are individual integrators' 'referencie' pages and the international trade directories (ATMIA, ATM Marketplace).
negative_findings.result_summary: No dedicated SK partner-directory surface located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without a national supplier directory, actor discovery for this cell must proceed vendor-by-vendor, which is slower and more likely to miss smaller processors and integrators.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For OEMs, search English plus Czech ('bankomaty', 'platební terminály') since CZ/SK are often served by one regional team and CZ material may name SK sites.

brief: For Slovakia, the supplier side splits cleanly into three tiers. Tier one is genuinely productive and SK-language: the acquiring JV Global Payments Slovensko (which publicly quantifies >37,000 terminals and >EUR 2bn annual volume), Printec Slovakia as the NCR/ATM channel (legally the former NCR Slovensko), Euronet as the independent ATM deployer, and SK integrators - Asseco Central Europe, Softec, Millennium, EEA - that publish named bank references covering core banking, card processing, branch systems and CRM. Tier two is the global OEMs (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, OpenWay), whose case-study libraries are rich for CEE but yielded no Slovakia-named deployment in this pass. The binding constraint is documented rather than incidental: SK business press reports that banks white-label vendor work and sometimes bar suppliers from naming them, so the highest-value SK-specific quantification is likely to come not from vendor marketing but from official filings - PMU merger decisions, EC case M.10378 on the three largest banks' JV, the NBS entity register, and ORSR/FinStat vendor accounts - with public procurement (UVO/TED) the largest untouched surface.
